chunks: From him, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Qasim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Ziyad, from Yaqub ibn Ja'far, who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah or Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the woman who performs lesbian acts with the woman; and he (peace be upon him) was reclining, so he sat up and said: 'Accursed! The rider as well as the ridden, until she comes out from their clothes, the rider as well as the ridden one, for Allah, Blessed and High, and the Angels, and the Guardians (peace be upon him) are cursing them both, and myself (peace be upon him), and the ones who remain in the loins of the men and the wombs of the women, for by Allah it is the greatest adultery, and by Allah, there is no repentance for them. May Allah kill Laqis, daughter of Iblees, with what she came up with.'

So the man said, 'This is what the people of Al-Iraq are coming up with'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah! It was happening upon the era of Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) before the existence of Al-Iraq, and regarding them Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May Allah curse the women resembling themselves with the men, and may Allah curse the men resembling themselves with the women'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on female lesbianism in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, the Imam (peace be upon him) elevates female lesbianism (tasaahq) to the status of 'the greatest adultery' (al-zina al-akbar), asserting that both the active and passive parties are cursed by Allah, the angels, and the Imams, with no repentance for them. He corrects the companion's attribution of this ruling to the people of Iraq by tracing it back to the Prophet's time, linking the act to the broader prophetic curse on gender imitation (tashabbuh), thereby establishing a strong theological and historical precedent for this specific juristic classification.
